Forged Promises, Broken Laws

By: Jana Marx | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A trusted lawyer weaves a web of deceit, forging legal documents and stealing millions from unsuspecting clients—leaving lives and fortunes in ruin.

Unique Selling Point:
The shocking abuse of trust by a lawyer who used her legal expertise to craft an intricate web of deception, defrauding her clients through sophisticated forgeries, fake legal documents, and false assurances. What sets this apart is the combination of high-level financial manipulation with the emotional impact on victims, who believed they were securing their futures, only to be devastated by someone they trusted implicitly.

Summary:
Zietta Janse van Rensburg, a once-trusted attorney in Malelane, used her legal expertise and position to orchestrate a series of elaborate frauds, targeting unsuspecting individuals and businesses with high-value property transactions and investment opportunities. Over the course of several years, she misappropriated millions of rands from her clients by fabricating legal documents, forging communications, and creating false identities.

In each case, Zietta leveraged her clients' trust by convincing them to invest large sums of money into property deals or investment projects, assuring them that she was handling the legal and financial aspects. Victims such as the Findlays, the Joneses, and Mr Patel were all duped into believing they were on the verge of securing valuable property or substantial financial returns. Zietta repeatedly used delaying tactics, making excuses about processing times, while providing fake proof of payments and title deeds to buy time and avoid suspicion.

Her schemes often involved the use of deceased individuals or non-existent legal entities, making the deals impossible to complete from the outset. In the end, none of the promised transactions materialised, and her victims were left financially and emotionally devastated, with over R14 million collectively missing and no property or investments to show for it. Zietta’s fraudulent activities came to light after years of deception, as multiple investigations revealed the depth of her crimes, leading to legal actions against her.

Press Release:


Fakes, Fraud and Forgeries
She was once a trusted attorney in Malelane, in Mpumlanga. Friends and clients alike used her legal expertise on various matters. But in the last few years, she’s allegedly used her position in the community, to orchestrate a series of elaborate frauds, targeting unsuspecting individuals and businesses with high-value property transactions and investment opportunities. Over the course of several years, she allegedly misappropriated millions of rands from her clients by fabricating legal documents, forging communications, and creating false identities. In each case, this well-known lawyer leveraged her clients' trust by convincing them to invest large sums of money into property deals or investment projects, assuring them that she was handling the legal and financial aspects. But she wasn’t. Instead, she’s left a trail of frustrated clients who say, she’s ruined their lives. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Jana Marx | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:



VO: In Malalane, Mpumalanga, some residents are fuming…

UPSOUND WILLIAM - 00:08:06:01 - 00:08:39:19

She represented a lot of the farmers, a lot of the community. Everybody trusted in her. There was no nobody that warned us

VO: Promised lucrative financial returns by someone they knew…

UPSOUND: FX3_3568
Bronwyn Findlay 10:04
I've trusted her. I believed her. I really did.

VO: But they’ve been left empty-handed…

UPSOUND FX3_3543
Joy Jones 19:48
I wish I would never have picked up that phone that day. Never.
20:28 She's ruined us.

VO: Allegedly betrayed by the attorney they trusted….

FROM LPC INTERVIEW
Govan Whittles 16:29
was a lot of money involved?

MABUDUSHA 16:30
A lot of money. We took him over 20 million…

VO: In Malalane, a small town on the edge of the Kruger National Park in Mpumalanga, retiree Joy Jones learnt the hard way, just how wild this area can be… and it had nothing to do with the animals….

UPSOUND | 00:23:50:04 - 00:24:11:16 - JOY
I just trust people and it just always bites me.

GOVAN: You think that's why she took advantage of you?

JOY: Definitely she was like a predator. I think she's like a predator.

VO: Joy’s story begins almost twenty years ago when she and her partner Alan Hilier decided to settle in this community. They bought a pub and started building a new life for themselves.

UPSOUND | 00:09:00:20 - 00:09:18:22 - JOY
It was just me and Alan and what we tried to do was create a proper pub. So we got the big screen going, we got the overhead projector, we would sleep in the pub at night.


UPSOUND | 00:09:22:16 - 00:09:28:19
GOVAN - Did you enjoy it?
JOY - We loved it. We loved, we loved it.


VO: Two years ago, Joy and Alan retired and sold their beloved pub. Within weeks, the transaction had been completed and funds from the sale of their business had been deposited into their account. A nest egg for the elderly couple… Then…

( PAUSE: ringing phone)

VO: …Twenty two days after they had sold the pub, Joy received the call that would upend all their plans…


UPSOUND | 25:26 - GOVAN: Describe that phone call to me.
JOY: Oh, Lord, if I could just erase that day.


VO: That was the day when Joy received an offer from this woman… Zietta Janse van Rensburg… a trusted attorney that she’d worked with before, with a long list of clients in Malalane…

UPSOUND | 00:06:38:23 - 00:06:44:22 - IRMA
Zieta is very popular Malalane. She was the town's lawyer.
She was a very likable person and I think everybody trusted her.

VO: Group Editor of Caxton Local Media, Irma Green started her investigation into Janse van Rensburg after several clients complained to the Legal Practice Council…

UPSOUND | 00:10:54:24 - 00:11:12:00 - GOVAN
So six LPC complaints come in, and you then decide to do some digging.. What did you find?

UPSOUND 00:11:12:00 - 00:11:33:19 – IRMA
Some of these, complaints were very intricate. It had layers to it.

00:11:33:20 - 00:12:13:06
IRMA: There were a lot of complaints about forged documents or, proof of payments.

VO: In Joy’s case, Janse van Rensburg offered a lucrative investment opportunity…

UPSOUND | 00:26:22:21 - 00:26:33:15 - JOY
She said, I'm desperately looking for, somebody to help me with, with 1.5 million. She said, I'm putting a million of my own.

VO: Janse van Rensburg urged Joy and Alan to invest R1.5 million into an alternative fuel scheme, where local companies were converting sugarcane into fuel. Janse van Rensburg promised the couple a 25 percent return on their investment, with interest and a further 2 percent shareholdings in a local fuel company.

UPSOUND Joy Jones 06:07
I said, Look, I'm going to have to speak to Allan… she said,, it's going to be good for the community, and it's going to create jobs..

VO: Joy transferred a million rand into Janse van Rensburg’s firm trust account. After all, in just six to eight weeks, the agreement was every cent would be repaid with interest… But it wasn’t…

LINK Attorneys are held to a higher standard of trust, but Zieta turned that trust into betrayal, exploiting the very people who depended on her.

VO: When William Findlay and his wife Bronwyn met Zieta Janse van Rensburg, they were impressed by the confident, well-spoken lawyer. William’s family owned a farm in Nelspruit that they were keen to subdivide. So, three years ago, they asked Janse van Rensburg to handle the paperwork to subdivide the farm.

UPSOUND: 00:10:20:05 - 00:10:43:01 - BRONWYN
She gave us two options. We could either leave the farm as agriculture, but then the value of the farm is less, or we can move the farm line because it is bordering town, move the farm land and then the farm value will be better. And I just thought she seems to know what she's talking about here.

VO: Despite her promises, for several months, Janse van Rensburg ALLEGEDLY failed to finalise the subdivision of the farm. Instead, she told the Findlays that she had secured them a buyer.

She claimed that the Department of Human Settlements were looking to purchase the land for R35 million to build affordable housing.

UPSOUND | 00:23:56:11 - 00:24:14:00 GOVAN
What did you think?
00:24:14:00 - 00:24:17:00
WILLIAM
Well, we were excited. That was a lot of money.

VO: Soon afterwards, Janse van Rensburg told William and Bronwyn that the Department had paid over the first tranche of seventeen million rands for the sale. They were eager to move on to the next chapter of their lives.

William Findlay 27:18
I spoke to and said to her listen, me and Bronwyn both have jobs. We want to buy this other farm in Lydenburg, so we have to resign.

William Findlay 28:32
She said, resign pack your bags. Start packing. Your money will be in your account the first of December.

28:04 - GOVAN
and you resigned on her word?
WILLIAM
we did after the proof that you gave us.

VO: Believing that they already had R17 Million rands waiting for them, the couple found a new property in Lydenburg, and Janse van Rensburg assured them, that she would pay the deposit on their new home, from her firm’s trust account… But the sellers never received the deposit.

UPSOUND - 00:35:27:07 - 00:35:37:01
GOVAN
Did Zita give bank guarantees for the purchase of the farm in Lydenburg?

WILLIAM: YES

00:35:37:03 - 00:36:00:22
GOVAN
Was that real?

BRONWYN
No.

WILLIAM
According to the the the lawyer firm that she gave the bank guarantees, they took it to ABSA. They see it. It's fake.

GOVAN But that was a farm that you had identified. That's the farm that we wanted to purchase.

WILLIAM
Yeah.

VO: The family would later discover that Janse van Rensburg, had been lying to them all along… She never finalised the subdivision of their farm and the Department of Human Settlements had never even offered to buy their property…


LPC 20:17 The mandate of the legal practice Council is that we need to uphold the integrity of the profession.

VO: Motlatso Mabudusha, the director of the Legal Practice Council in Mpumalanga says that they received several complaints concerning Janse van Rensburg. It was enough to launch their own investigation.

UPSOUND 20:00 – MABUDUSHA
So most of our complaints ranged and charges ranged from misappropriation, failure to account, failure to deal with matter properly, failure to advise clients or keep clients interest.

GOVAN
Are those serious charges?

MABUDUSHA
Very serious charges that could result in one being removed from the roll.

VO: The LPC explained that as the conveyancer responsible for the transfer of property, Janse van Rensburg would represent property sellers or buyers in the transactions.

But during the transfer process, one of the parties wouldn’t receive payment. Janse van Rensburg, though, would provide documents as proof of payment. The clients soon learnt that these documents were fake.

Govan Whittles 13:26
How many were there?

MABUDUSHA 13:32
We looking at more than 10. More than 10 complaints.

Govan Whittles 14:07
Were these were these frivolous complaints?

MABUDUSHA 14:11
her? With her? Specifically, none of them were. They were all serious complaints.

Govan Whittles 16:29
was a lot of money involved?

MABUDUSHA 16:30
A lot of money. We took him over 20 million…

VO: Earlier this year, the LPC’s investigation into the allegations against Janse van Rensburg resulted in her suspension. But Janse van Rensburg wasn’t deterred, and she continued to represent clients…

VO: Then the LPC shut down her firm. It’s now proceeding with its application to have her struck off the role. But in the meantime, with a long list of allegations and after several requests for an interview, we tracked down Janse van Rensburg to her home.

UPSOUND Zietta: Zietta hello?

UPSOUND Govan: Hi Zietta?

UPSOUND Zietta: Yes?

UPSOUND Govan: It’s Govan Whittles from Carte Blanche.

UPSOUND Zietta: I’m not home.

UPSOUND Govan: We’re trying to contact you, Zietta, could you speak to us, please, and do an interview?

UPSOUND Zietta: Not now I’m not home.

UPSOUND Govan: She hung up. I don’t think anyone has ever dropped the phone on me from the gate before…

VO: Janse van Rensburg failed to respond to any of our queries other than to claim there’s a conspiracy against her. She’s using a podcast to push back against her alleged detractors.

1;01 I've been bound by attorney client privilege, unable to expose the skeletons I personally buried for them. In the media I am left next to the grave with the shovel in hand, alone.

VO: The Findlays say they lost almost a million rand in income, and incurred substantial debt in the process.

But for William, his family lost far more than money…

CLIP 3569 - UPSOUND - William:
We lost our our dreams, our promises to our kids for their future.

VO: Meanwhile Joy and Alan’s new lawyers forced Janse van Rensburg to repay their million rand… but not before the couple had put themselves into serious debt while they waited for their lucrative investment…

Clip 3545 - UPSOUND - Joy Jones 13:39
8;46 This was our last chance to have a good few golden years.

LINK – 5:17
Usually, scammers have a type but, in this case, Zieta targeted everyone – business people, the elderly, even farmers and it’s not so much about the money that they lost, it’s about the fact that she wrecked people’s live. | That’s why justice is so important in this case….

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A trusted lawyer weaves a web of deceit, forging legal documents and stealing millions from unsuspecting clients—leaving lives and fortunes in ruin.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The shocking abuse of trust by a lawyer who used her legal expertise to craft an intricate web of deception, defrauding her clients through sophisticated forgeries, fake legal documents, and false assurances. What sets this apart is the combination of high-level financial manipulation with the emotional impact on victims, who believed they were securing their futures, only to be devastated by someone they trusted implicitly.
metadata.Summary: Zietta Janse van Rensburg, a once-trusted attorney in Malelane, used her legal expertise and position to orchestrate a series of elaborate frauds, targeting unsuspecting individuals and businesses with high-value property transactions and investment opportunities. Over the course of several years, she misappropriated millions of rands from her clients by fabricating legal documents, forging communications, and creating false identities. In each case, Zietta leveraged her clients' trust by convincing them to invest large sums of money into property deals or investment projects, assuring them that she was handling the legal and financial aspects. Victims such as the Findlays, the Joneses, and Mr Patel were all duped into believing they were on the verge of securing valuable property or substantial financial returns. Zietta repeatedly used delaying tactics, making excuses about processing times, while providing fake proof of payments and title deeds to buy time and avoid suspicion. Her schemes often involved the use of deceased individuals or non-existent legal entities, making the deals impossible to complete from the outset. In the end, none of the promised transactions materialised, and her victims were left financially and emotionally devastated, with over R14 million collectively missing and no property or investments to show for it. Zietta’s fraudulent activities came to light after years of deception, as multiple investigations revealed the depth of her crimes, leading to legal actions against her.
